run.note: Full run on the tree's 1.63.0, which IS published on nuget.org (the published latest is 1.63.0), so the global tool was really force-updated. The tree was built, packed for osx-arm64 and installed into a scratch --tool-path as well; the two builds' tool surfaces are identical. Every lane ran its own --data-root and its own --port 0 server. The live bank was read, never written: one VACUUM INTO copy for the real-scale long-query measurement. The 70,763-entry v17 eval bank was copied for the pre-cap control (1.56.0 cannot open a v19 bank). One item fails: reserved-name-registration-is-not-refused, a gap found while running the shared item on 1.63.0 and carried unchanged by the 2.0.0 branch (PR #909). The failing item was re-verified live on the 2.0.0 branch head 99ef8b8c: the mint is refused and a bank that already holds the private name row blocks the target and publishes nothing. Two branch observations are recorded as findings (the settings endpoint's 500 on the blocked state, and the source-build model artifact that nearly became a false regression report).

derived.note: Produced by scripts/derive-facts.py at run time, never typed from memory or a previous run.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: status pass, accepted: 'the vector leg is live only after the embedding engine is set, and with it the semantically-related note (no substantive word overlap with the query) ranks first on a vector leg'.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: The verdict holds but the item could not have failed. The note's text ('A brass astrolabe catches the lamplight inside the observatory dome, ... against the evening sky.') shares the words 'inside' and 'evening' with the query ('an antique navigation instrument reflecting evening light inside a stargazing room'), so the FTS leg matched the note on its own and the note would have been found - and ranked first - on a build with a dead vector leg. The prior run never ran the keyword-only control, so nothing in its evidence separated the two legs.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: This run, on a fresh bank: content 'Brass astrolabe, lamplight glowing over the observatory dome; engraved ring turns slowly beneath night sky.' (no query token at all, not even the article 'a' - the FTS plan's OR join is built from the raw tokens, so a one-letter word in the content is enough to give the keyword leg a hit), query unchanged. The note ranks 1 with 'legs: [{legName: vector, rank 1}]', 'cosine: 0.844', 'participatingLegs: [vector]'; the same query with vectorWeight 0 returns 'results: []'; sqlite 'SELECT count(*) FROM entries_fts WHERE entries_fts MATCH <the OR expression>' returns 0.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: 'A semantic query must be one that keyword match cannot carry' is a property of the CONTENT, not of the query. A content that shares a common word with the query - even one the writer considered unrelated - hands the hit to the keyword leg and quietly disarms the item. The control (the same query with vectorWeight 0) is what proves the vector leg carried it, and it costs one call.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: accepted: 'the eval-bank timings (11.6 s / 10.6 s) reproduce the 1.59.0 run's 12.0 s cold on the same bank; the live-bank copy is smaller (25,243 entries) and answers in 1.84 s / 0.56 s' and the item's own clause 'the stopword run times out'.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: The like-for-like comparison the prior run describes does not exist in its evidence: the 1.59.0 and 1.61.1 numbers were measured on the eval bank, the pre-cap control's 22.2 s / 28.2 s on a second copy of it, and the 1.84 s / 0.56 s on the live bank - three banks, no pair measured on the same one. This run measured both builds on the same 70,763-entry bank: 1.63.0 answers the two pastes in 1.17 s and 0.56 s, 1.56.0 in 14.72 s and 13.11 s. The 'times out' clause is a property of the client timeout, not of the build: at a 60 s timeout the pre-cap build answers in 13.1 s, and at a 10 s timeout it times out while the capped build answers in 0.56 s.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: Same eval bank, same two pastes, same client: 1.63.0 -> 1.17 s / 0.56 s, warning 'Keyword (FTS) matching is capped too: it searches only the first 64 distinct words of a query this long.'; 1.56.0 -> 14.72 s / 13.11 s, warning 'Keyword (FTS) matching still searches the query in full.'; at a 10 s client timeout -> '1.56.0 stopword paste TIMED OUT after 10.0s: ReadTimeout'.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: A cost comparison between two builds is only a claim about the pair of builds if both ran on the same bank with the same client settings. Three banks across three runs cannot be compared to each other, and a timeout clause needs its timeout stated, because the same build answers in 13 s and times out at 10 s.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: status substituted, accepted: 'a scratch --tool-path install of a local pack instead of a global force-update from nuget. ... Publishing 1.61.1 needs the owner's publish.yml dispatch'.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: The substitution was correct for 1.61.1 - that version was never published - but it is not a property of the checklist: 1.63.0 IS on nuget.org, so the global force-update is a plain pass this time ('Tool 'ai-raccoon' (version '1.63.0') was successfully uninstalled.' then '... was successfully installed.'; ai-raccoon --version -> 1.63.0+d06746fc). The tree carries three commits past the published release commit, and none of them touches src/, tests/ or scripts/, so the published binary and the tree's own pack are the same product - the two builds' 30-tool surfaces are identical.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: 'git diff --stat d06746fc..HEAD -- src/ tests/ scripts/' -> empty; global build tools/list 30 names, tree build tools/list 30 names, 'only in global: []', 'only in tree: []'.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: The substituted verdict belonged to that release, not to this item. Reading it as 'the global tool cannot be force-updated' would have kept a substitution in place for a release that does not need one.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-run: this run, item long-query-keyword-terms-capped (a procedure note for the next run)
findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: none - a hazard found while running this checklist, not a verdict in an earlier one.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: A bank copy carries the owner's WATCH REGISTRATIONS, and the copy's watcher digests the real directories those registrations name. The live copy had its watches deleted before it was served, but the eval copy for the 1.63.0 comparison was served first (the server had to migrate it from v17 to v19, and the migration holds the write lock), and its log shows 'Watch for project ai-badger at /Users/arasz/RiderProjects/ai-badger digested again after a failure' three times before the watches were deleted. The reads are of the owner's own files into a scratch copy, so nothing was damaged, but a checklist that copies a live bank should clear the copy's watches BEFORE serving it - and must not serve a copy it still needs to migrate.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: ck/evalcopy2/serve.log: 'Watch for project ai-badger at /Users/arasz/RiderProjects/ai-badger digested again after a failure; scanning it for changed files' (3 lines). The first tool call against that server was refused: '"project_id_token_get" refused: bank-busy: the bank is busy (another writer holds the lock); retry the call'.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: Two things in one: clear the copy's watches before serving, and expect 'bank-busy' on the first call after a schema migration - it is a refusal with a retry instruction, not a hang.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-run: this run, against PR #909 head 99ef8b8c (a near-miss regression report, caught before it was sent)
findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: none - a candidate finding this run withdrew after checking it against the same build of the base branch.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: A build from source answers every write and every search with 'unexpected-error: EmbeddingModelRejectedException' instead of degrading to FTS5-only. The cause is the build, not the branch: the bundled model's 92.9 MB model_fp16.onnx_data is not in git, so a 'git archive' build has an incomplete Models directory and the chunk-budget resolution throws while loading the manifest. 1.63.0 built from source fails identically ('unexpected-error: EmbeddingModelRejectedException' for both add_memory and memory_search), and the published tool ships the data file.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: branch build (2.0.0): 'Manifest .../Models/granite-embedding-small-english-r2/ai-raccoon.manifest.json declares file model_fp16.onnx_data but it is missing from ...'. 1.63.0 built the same way: the same refusal on the same call. The installed 1.63.0 tool has 'model_fp16.onnx_data 92.9M' in its Models directory and answers the same search with the documented warning 'memory engine not configured - the memory section is FTS5-only'.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: Comparing a source build of a branch against the installed build of the base is not a like-for-like comparison: the model files differ, and the difference shows up as an opaque 'unexpected-error'. Before reporting a regression, build the BASE the same way and run the same call - the defect has to be in the branch, not in the build.

findings-against-prior-runs.prior-claim: none - an observation on the branch, not a verdict in an earlier run.
findings-against-prior-runs.what-is-actually-true: The new name clause makes the settings CLI answer 500 on a bank that holds a private 'shared' name row: 'settings ingest scope add shared <path>' and 'settings watch enable shared true' both answer 'the settings server at http://127.0.0.1:51090/mcp failed with 500 Internal Server Error - this is a server-side fault, not a bad argument'. The refusal underneath is correct and explicit ('shared-project-conflict: legacy private data or registration uses 'shared'; repair that owner before using the reserved target. No data was published.'), and the MCP path answers the same state as invalid-argument; only the settings endpoint lets the ArgumentException escape as an unhandled fault.
findings-against-prior-runs.evidence: ck/branchB/serve-new.log: 'System.ArgumentException: shared-project-conflict: ... No data was published. at AiRaccoon.Infrastructure.Sqlite.SharedProjectStorage.RequireSharedAvailableAsync ... at AiRaccoon.Settings.SettingsEndpoint.RefuseProjectAsync ... at AiRaccoon.Settings.SettingsEndpoint.MapSettings'.
findings-against-prior-runs.so-what: A refusal that reaches the user as '500 - server-side fault, not a bad argument' is worse than the refusal it carries: the caller is told to retry a server bug instead of to repair the private owner. Mapping that one ArgumentException to 400 in the settings endpoint is a small change.

items.expected-result: Release build and pack succeed; the global ai-raccoon tool force-updates to this build and `ai-raccoon --version` matches derived.version
items.command: dotnet build -c Release; python3 scripts/download-mlx-runtime.py; dotnet pack src/AiRaccoon/AiRaccoon.csproj -c Release -p:RuntimeIdentifiers=osx-arm64 -o $S/artifacts; dotnet tool install ai-raccoon --version 1.63.0 --add-source $S/artifacts --tool-path $S/tool; $S/tool/ai-raccoon --version; dotnet tool uninstall -g ai-raccoon; dotnet tool install -g ai-raccoon --version 1.63.0; ai-raccoon --version; git diff --stat d06746fc..HEAD -- src/ tests/ scripts/; tools/list on the global build and on the tree build, diffed
items.evidence: Build: 'ok dotnet build: 8 projects, 0 errors, 0 warnings (00:00:27.64)'. Pack: 'Successfully created package .../ai-raccoon.osx-arm64.1.63.0.nupkg' and 'ai-raccoon.1.63.0.nupkg'. Scratch install of the local pack: 'Tool ai-raccoon (version 1.63.0) was successfully installed'; $S/tool/ai-raccoon --version -> '1.63.0+cf5466fc119898995f0ee1a0483ccc7687e5dceb' (the tree HEAD). Global force-update: 'Tool 'ai-raccoon' (version '1.63.0') was successfully uninstalled.' then 'Tool 'ai-raccoon' (version '1.63.0') was successfully installed.'; ai-raccoon --version -> '1.63.0+d06746fcf59734f5000a657f026a9eca8ee40608' (the published 1.63.0, commit d06746fc). Product-code diff between the published commit and the tree: 'git diff --stat d06746fc..HEAD -- src/ tests/ scripts/' -> empty. Tool surfaces: global build 30 tools, tree build 30 tools, 'only in global: []', 'only in tree: []'. SIDE EFFECT, recorded honestly: the global uninstall+install removed the tool's install directory, and the running host's install watchdog (ADR-0116) shut the user's own server down with it - the listener on 7721 changed pid (23884 -> 48124, started 01:24:26) and a new host came up on 7721 answering 401 without a token. The bank was not touched (~/.ai-raccoon/memory.db, identity-key and mcp-token all still in place). This run never bound or issued a --restart against 7721 itself.
items.observed-result: The running binaries report the derived version 1.63.0. The global tool is the published 1.63.0 (d06746fc) and the tree carries three further commits that touch no product code (only .ai-badger scaffolding and docs), so the two builds are the same product. Both expose exactly the same 30 MCP tools. The global force-update is not side-effect free: reinstalling the tool cycles the user's running server on the default port through the install watchdog. The port was not bound by this run, but the user's server was cycled by it.
items.acceptance-reason: A plain pass this time: 1.63.0 is published on nuget, so the global force-update is a real uninstall+install of the release rather than a scratch substitute. The version comparison against the derived facts holds, and the two builds' tool surfaces are identical, which is what makes the rest of the run a statement about 1.63.0. Accepted with the side effect above named: the item asks for a real global force-update, and that is what cycles a server started from the tool's own install directory.

Wait for three watch_files rows and leave node_modules readable (a `chmod 000` decoy is absent whether or not it is excluded, so that leg could never fail), wait 2 s, then edit y.md so watches.last_change_ts moves past x.md's watch_files.updated_at. Read both values while the server runs, because a stopped WAL bank will not open read-only. Stop the server. Replace one word of x.md with a new term of the same byte length and `touch -t $(date -r <t> +%Y%m%d%H%M.%S)` it, where t is between x.md's updated_at and last_change_ts. Rewrite w.md at a different size with a new term, and touch it to before its own updated_at. Restart on the same data root. Within seconds memory_search finds both new terms, watch_files shows new updated_at and size for x.md and w.md, and memory_watch_status reads Healthy. Neither the node_modules term nor the .git term is ever found. Premise: before the restart, updated_at(x.md) <= mtime(x.md) <= last_change_ts. A build without ADR-0121 finds neither new term, because it re-queues only files with mtime > last_change_ts. The 5-minute heal pass (WatchHostedService.HealInterval, event 322 at Debug) is optional: it needs a server left up for over 5 minutes (ADR-0121)

items.expected-result: ADR-0137: the reserved target's 'registration is an idempotent no-op and cannot rename it', and 'Existing private rows, workspaces, code or registration under literal `shared` block the target without publishing them'. So minting a project under the reserved literal NAME must not create a second, private 'shared' - and if it does, the reserved target must refuse to activate over it.
items.command: fresh scratch bank ck/shared2: project_id_token_get {name: 'shared'} FIRST; then project_id_get {name: 'shared'}; then 'settings ingest scope add shared <docs>', 'settings watch enable shared true', memory_watch_add {projectId: 'shared', path: <docs>}; memory_search {projectId: 'shared', scope: 'all'}; memory_stats {projectId: 'shared'}; then read the projects table of the scratch bank
items.evidence: Mint: '{"data": {"projectId": "01a160f4-e80e-77d8-803a-6d171e7589d3", ...}}' - a NEW private guid, not the reserved target. Name lookup after the mint: '{"data": {"projectId": "shared"}}' - the reserved id, so the private project is unreachable by name. The target then activated anyway: memory_watch_add -> '{"projectId": "shared", "path": ".../shared-docs", "pruned": []}'; memory_search -> the handbook document; memory_stats -> '{"entries": 1, "pending": 1, "contexts": ["shared"]}'. The projects table holds both kinds of state: '[('01a160f4-e80e-77d8-803a-6d171e7589d3', 'shared', 1792628025)]' - a private project registered under the reserved NAME, while the reserved target published a document. The activation guard that is supposed to stop this (src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure/Sqlite/SharedProjectStorage.cs, RequireSharedAvailableAsync) tests 'EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM projects WHERE id = @projectId)' - the reserved ID, not the name - so a name-registered private owner passes it.
items.observed-result: Minting the name 'shared' is not the idempotent no-op ADR-0137 specifies: it registers a second, private project that no name lookup can ever find again, and the reserved target activates and publishes over it instead of being blocked. The ADR's sentence admits two readings - a registration under the literal id 'shared' (which the implementation covers, and which is the legacy case) or one under the literal name (which the product's own mint tool creates today) - and the code implements only the first.
items.acceptance-reason: Not accepted as specified: either the mint must refuse the reserved name (an idempotent no-op returning the reserved id, which is what ADR-0137 says), or the guard must key on the name as well as the id. Today the product can create, in one call, the exact state the ADR says blocks the target - and then leaves a project that is invisible to project_id_get. The fix is cheap in 2.0.0, where this tool is renamed to save_project_id_token and the rename is already a breaking change; on the PR #909 branch the same mint path is carried over unchanged.

remediation.fixed-in: PR #909 (ai-raccoon 2.0.0), branch head 99ef8b8c 'fix: the reserved shared name cannot be minted into a private project'
remediation.verified-live: yes - the branch was built from a git archive of 99ef8b8c and both legs were driven over MCP, not read from the diff
remediation.lane-a-clean-bank: save_project_id_token {name: 'shared'} -> 'invalid-argument: reserved-name: 'shared' is the reserved shared target; it needs no minted id and cannot be registered under another id. Nothing was registered.' The name 'Shared' (different case) is still accepted and mints normally - the refusal is exact and case-sensitive, as stated. The reserved target still works on that clean bank: add_watch {projectId: 'shared'} -> accepted, and the watch registered the shared-docs path.
remediation.lane-b-bank-that-already-holds-the-priva: The private 'shared' name row was minted by the 1.63.0 build (the behaviour the branch removes), and the 2.0.0 build then opened that same bank: add_watch, query and get_store_statistics all refuse with 'invalid-argument: shared-project-conflict: legacy private data or registration uses 'shared'; repair that owner before using the reserved target. No data was published.' and the bank holds 0 entries - nothing was published over the private owner. The projects table after the 1.63.0 mint: [('01a1611c-82d8-7ff8-8059-547b4e35615f', 'shared', 1792630620)].
remediation.residual-note: On that same blocked bank the CLI path answers differently from the MCP path: 'settings ingest scope add shared <path>' and 'settings watch enable shared true' answer 'ai-raccoon: the settings server at http://127.0.0.1:51090/mcp failed with 500 Internal Server Error - this is a server-side fault, not a bad argument'. The server log shows the good refusal (shared-project-conflict) escaping SettingsEndpoint.RefuseProjectAsync as an unhandled ArgumentException, so the settings endpoint's error mapping turns a refusal into a 500 and the CLI blames the server for what is a bad argument. The MCP path answers the same state correctly as invalid-argument.
